title: Promise and Kitchen
premise: Kestrel Thackeray keeps her late grandfather's lighthouse on a windswept island, writing novels under a pseudonym and guarding her heart as carefully as the light. When a November storm strands her ex-fiancé, ferry captain Elias Marsh, and his business rival—and her former editor—Jonah Reyes at the lighthouse for nine days, old betrayals and unfinished love surface alongside a discovery: her grandfather's will left the lighthouse to whoever can prove they'll keep it burning. As the rivals' feud entangles Kestrel's inheritance and her secret manuscript, she must choose between the safe small life she built and the whole-hearted risk of loving Elias again—choosing him at last as the final ferry of the season pulls away without them.
about_author: Theo Underhill is the pen name of a former coastal radio archivist who spent a decade collecting storm logs and keeper's diaries from decommissioned lighthouses along the North Atlantic. Promise and Kitchen is their third novel, written in winter, in sight of water.

chapters.title: The Last Light Before Winter
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She tends the automated lighthouse her grandfather once kept by hand, cataloguing her quiet routines and hiding her finished manuscript in a bread tin. Emotional beat: contentment that feels suspiciously like hiding.

chapters.title: Ferry Weather
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Ferry captain Elias Marsh charts his final seasonal crossing to Thackeray Island, dreading and craving a glimpse of the woman he left seven years ago. Emotional beat: guilt sharpened into longing.

chapters.title: A Manuscript in a Bread Tin
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Her agent calls: an anonymous submission of her novel has reached Jonah Reyes, the celebrated editor who once gutted her confidence in college. Panic; she considers burning it. Emotional beat: terror of being seen.

chapters.title: Two Men on One Dock
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The last scheduled ferry arrives carrying both Elias and Jonah, who are rivals over a coastal development deal that would shutter the island's harbor. Kestrel watches them argue from the keeper's cottage window. Emotional beat: dread arriving on schedule.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The storm hits early; the ferry can't return, phones fail, and three strangers become housemates. She lights the backup generator and the old oil lamp out of superstition. Emotional beat: forced intimacy beginning.

chapters.title: Kitchen Hours
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Trapped indoors, Kestrel cooks from her grandmother's recipe book while Elias chops wood and Jonah edits pages he pretends not to recognize. Emotional beat: warmth that neither rival trusts.

chapters.title: What Elias Broke
chapters.summary: Flashback woven through present scene, Kestrel's POV. Seven years ago Elias chose his father's shipping company over their engagement, believing he was saving her from poverty. Emotional beat: understanding without absolution.

chapters.title: The Editor's Confession
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah admits he recognized Kestrel's voice in the anonymous manuscript weeks ago and came to the island partly to find her. He offers to publish it—as long as she leaves the island to promote it. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as rescue.

chapters.title: Rival Terms
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias discovers Jonah's development deal includes buying the lighthouse land; Jonah discovers Elias has been quietly blocking it. Their truce fractures over cards and whiskey. Emotional beat: two men fighting over a woman's home like territory.

chapters.title: Grandfather's Will
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Searching the attic for storm shutters, she finds her grandfather's will: the lighthouse goes to whoever 'keeps the light'—a clause vague enough to be a trap or a gift. Emotional beat: inheritance as question, not answer.

chapters.title: Nine Days In
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Midway through the stranding, routines soften into something like family: shared meals, card games, Kestrel reading her novel aloud by lamplight. Both men fall harder. Emotional beat: the dangerous comfort of almost.

chapters.title: Lent Pieces
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Elias asks for a second chance; Jonah asks her to choose herself and the city. Kestrel realizes she has spent years lending pieces of her heart so no one could break the whole. Emotional beat: naming her own pattern.

chapters.title: The Storm Log
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Reading her grandfather's storm logs, Elias finds entries proving the old man knew about the engagement and approved of him—a letter never delivered. Emotional beat: grief for time lost to silence.

chapters.title: First Kiss, Second Mistake
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Elias's POV alternating. During a blackout, Kestrel and Elias kiss in the lamp room; Jonah sees them descend hand in hand. Emotional beat: joy immediately taxed with consequence.

chapters.title: Jonah's Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Wounded but principled, Jonah withdraws the development bid entirely and tells Kestrel the truth: publishing her book means leaving, and he won't pretend otherwise. Emotional beat: love expressed as letting go.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. With the storm clearing, Kestrel confronts what staying costs—the island is dying, the grant money gone, and love alone doesn't pay for lamp oil. Emotional beat: romance colliding with economics.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: All three POV. The icebreaker escort arrives; Jonah boards with her manuscript under his arm, promising nothing except publication. Elias stays on the dock, refusing to ask her to stay. Emotional beat: the choice made visible.

chapters.title: Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. At the gangway, Kestrel hands Jonah the manuscript to publish—but boards the ferry only to walk its length and step back off onto the island, choosing Elias and the hard life openly. Emotional beat: risk taken in full view.

chapters.title: Keeping the Light
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias reveals he sold his stake in his father's company to fund the harbor cooperative, dissolving the rivalry honestly. Together they petition to keep the lighthouse manned under the will's clause. Emotional beat: duty remade as shared purpose.

chapters.title: Proof of Burning
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A hearing on the mainland; Kestrel speaks publicly for the first time, claiming authorship of her novel and her island in one breath. The commission grants the lighthouse protected status. Emotional beat: invisibility ended by voice.

chapters.title: Promise and Kitchen
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Spring returns; the published novel arrives in a box, dedicated to 'the ones who stayed.' Elias fixes the kitchen table where everything was decided. Emotional beat: ordinary happiness earned, not granted.

chapters.title: The First Ferry of Spring
chapters.summary: Multiple POV closing epilogue. The season's first ferry brings tourists, letters from readers, and a postcard from Jonah wishing them well. Kestrel lights the lamp at dusk beside Elias. Emotional beat: the light kept, the heart kept, both by choice.
